lines: Hello. Keep your voice easy. The village has had enough sharp sounds.
Good to see someone walking calmly. We have had our fill of running.
If you are here to help, start by closing gates behind you.
Careful where you step. Everyone is still a little quick to turn their head.
The village is standing, but it has not settled yet.
Speak softly today. Even the walls feel tired.
If you came with steady hands, they are welcome.
We are counting people, checking doors, and trying to breathe again.
The danger passed, but it left its shadow behind.
Stay alert. Peace feels thin after a day like that.
The shop is open again, though I still look up at every sudden sound.
We put the tools back in place after checking the doors twice.
Work feels strange when the alarm is still fresh in your ears.
I am here, but part of me is still watching the road.
The village is safe enough to work and tense enough to notice everything.
I lost time to the danger, so today's chores have piled up.
A quiet customer is welcome after all that noise.
The damage is repaired. My nerves are taking longer.
I kept the door unlatched today in case the bell rings again.
Tell me what you need while I still have a calm moment.
I am watching the roads today. Talk if you need to, but keep one eye open.
If trouble comes back, I would rather meet it standing.
The village is still here. That means we still have something worth guarding.
I do not plan to be caught unready twice.
There is <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray> in the village, yes. There is also backbone.
If something comes through that gate, it will find us awake.
I have no interest in hiding while others stand in front.
The quiet feels thin today. I am listening through it.
Stay close to the paths and do not ignore the bell.
We are not helpless just because we were frightened.
The alarm rope is clear, and I moved the spare shields closer to the square.
I checked every gate hinge before breakfast. None of them will catch if we need to close up fast.
I checked the outer paths before coming back to the square.
The village is calm because someone stayed awake last night.
I keep my tools close when the road has been too quiet.
If the bell rings, I know which door I am guarding first.
Courage is useful. Knowing when to call for help is better.
I have already made sure the children know where to run.
We can talk while I keep an eye on the gate.
Nothing looks wrong yet, and I intend to keep it that way.
